;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[November 2019 Syria bombings]]
**A [[car bomb]] detonates in [[Tell Abyad]], [[Raqqa Governorate]], killing ten people and wounding 25 others. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security/car-bomb-kills-at-least-10-people-near-syrias-border-with-turkey-idUSKBN1XX0BS?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Colombian protests]]
**Three [[National Police of Colombia|Colombian police]] are killed and seven wounded by a car bomb in [[Santander de Quilichao]], [[Cauca Department|Cauca]] province. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/23/colombian-protests-flare-again-as-looting-erupts-in-bogota (''The Guardian'')]

;Health and environment
*[[2019 Samoa measles outbreak]]
**[[Tonga]] and [[Fiji]] declare a [[state of emergency]] as part of an ongoing [[measles]] outbreak. Conditions worsen in [[Samoa]] where the death toll continues to rise and schools remain closed. There are 1,797 confirmed cases as of Saturday, with 153 detected on Friday alone. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-50528834 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[2019–2020 Iranian protests|2019 Iranian fuel protests]]
**[[Iran|Iranian]] [[Vice President of Iran|Vice President]] [[Eshaq Jahangiri]] warns regional states of dire consequences, claiming the protests are "directly linked to the [[United States]], [[Saudi Arabia]], and [[Israel]]." [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-gasoline-protests/iran-warns-regional-states-of-consequences-if-they-stoked-unrest-idUSKBN1XX07O (Reuters)]
*[[Iran–Iraq relations]]
**The [[Iran-Iraq border|border between]] Iran and [[Iraq]] reopens, after being closed for a week due to mass protests in their [[2019–2020 Iranian protests|respective]] [[2019 Iraqi protests|countries]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-iran-border/iraq-iran-border-crossing-reopens-after-week-long-closure-statement-idUSKBN1XX0BB?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[China–United States relations]]
**[[China|Chinese]] [[Foreign Minister of the People's Republic of China|Foreign Affairs Minister]] [[Wang Yi (politician)|Wang Yi]] accuses the United States of being the "world's biggest destabilizing factor" and of "smearing China everywhere" at the [[G20]] meeting in [[Nagoya]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-usa-trade/china-attacks-u-s-at-g20-as-the-worlds-biggest-source-of-instability-idUSKBN1XX09P?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Australia–China relations]], [[Chinese intelligence activity abroad]]
**[[Australia]]n network newspapers, [[Nine Entertainment Co.|Nine]]’s ''The Age'' and ''[[Sydney Morning Herald]]'' newspapers, report that a Chinese spy, [[Wang Liqiang|Wang ‘William’ Liqiang]] - who defected to Australia, gives counter-espionage agency the names of senior military intelligence officers he says funded and conducted operations in Hong Kong, Taiwan and Australia. [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3039046/chinese-spy-who-infiltrated-hong-kong-taiwan-defects-australia (''South China Morning Post'')]
**Wang says he was personally involved in infiltration and disruption operations in all three territories, and “revealed in granular detail” how Beijing covertly controls listed companies to fund intelligence operations, including the surveillance and profiling of dissidents and the co-opting of media organizations. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-50528831 (BBC News)]
**Wang is now seeking asylum in Australia, saying he ‘will be dead’ if he returns home. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-11-23/chinese-spy-wang-liqiang-seeks-political-asylum-australia-report/11732174 (ABC)]
** The Shanghai police department says that Wang is a conman who was convicted for fraud in 2016 and is being investigated for another case of fraud since April 2019. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3039101/self-proclaimed-chinese-spy-william-wang-who-defected (''South China Morning Post'')]
* [[List of pastoral visits of Pope Francis|Pope Francis travels to Japan]]
**During his  23 to 26 November journey to [[Japan]], [[Pope Francis]] visits [[Tokyo]], [[Nagasaki]] and [[Hiroshima]]. The only pope to previously visit Japan was [[Pope John Paul II]] from 23–26 February 1981. [https://press.vatican.va/content/salastampa/en/bollettino/pubblico/2019/10/28/191028a.html (Holy See Press Office)] [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/vatican-city/news/2019-11/pope-john-paul-ii-visit-japan-1981.html (Vatican News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Bougainvillean independence referendum]]
**People in the [[Autonomous Region of Bougainville]] vote to choose between more [[autonomy]] within [[Papua New Guinea]] or outright [[independence]]. However, the [[Government of Papua New Guinea|Papua New Guinea]] central government will have the final say on accepting independence. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/403929/expectations-high-as-bougainville-referendum-gets-underway (RNZ)]
*[[2019 referendum on the creation of a Sidama region]]
**The [[Ethiopia]]n [[National Election Board of Ethiopia|electoral board]] announces that the [[referendum]] to grant autonomy to the [[Sidama Zone]] passed with 98.5% of the vote. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ethiopia-politics/ethiopias-sidama-vote-overwhelmingly-to-form-autonomous-region-idUSKBN1XX0GR?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Climate change policy of the United States|Climate change policy]], [[Harvard-Yale football game]]
**A non-violent protest was held at the [[Yale Bowl]] during the annual [[Harvard]]-[[Yale]] [[American football|football]] game at halftime. The apparently scheduled protest included both Yale and Harvard students. The students were protesting the colleges' usage of endowments from [[fossil fuel]] companies. The game was delayed for about an hour. There were some arrests. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/11/23/us/harvard-yale-climate-protest-trnd/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/23/us/harvard-yale-game-protest.html (''The New York Times''}]

;Sports
*[[2019 Copa Libertadores]]
**The premier [[association football]] club competition of South America concludes with [[Brazil|Brazilian]] club [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] beating titleholders [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] 2-1 in [[Lima]]'s [[Estadio Monumental "U"|Monumental Stadium]]. It is their first title since 1981 and second overall. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50532892 (BBC Sport)]
